grclanker v0.1.4 rides out rate limits and brief outages: 32 integrations and the KEV, EPSS, CMVP, SCF, and FedRAMP tools now retry rate limits, server errors, and timeouts, and a read that still fails is reported as unread, so no check passes on partial data. Access checks say so when a vendor rejects your credentials, the first run is smoother, and installs are safer: a failed upgrade puts the previous install or skill back, and every release bundle now runs on its own operating system before it is published. `kevs_search` puts an exact CVE ID first, and the Zendesk, LaunchDarkly, AWS, and SCF tools now do what their docs say. The tool surface is unchanged: `grclanker tools` still reports 241 domain tools and 7 compute backend tools.

## Retries and incomplete reads

- **Rate limits and outages are retried.** 32 integrations now retry a rate limit, a server error, a timeout, or a network failure before giving up, three to five attempts in all by default. The 32 are Ansible Automation Platform, AWS, Azure, Box, Cloudflare, CrowdStrike, Datadog, Duo, Elastic, GitHub, Google Cloud, Google Workspace, KnowBe4, LaunchDarkly, MuleSoft, New Relic, Okta, PagerDuty, Palo Alto Networks, Qualys, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Slack, Snowflake, Splunk, Tenable, Vanta, Veracode, Webex, Zendesk, Zoom, and Zscaler. Before, Ansible Automation Platform, Azure, Cloudflare, Google Cloud, and Vanta retried nothing, and Duo, Okta, Slack, Webex, and Zoom retried only a rate limit.
- **Azure, Google Cloud, and AWS.** Azure and Google Cloud give every request, token requests included, up to 4 attempts, and retry a 429, 500, 502, 503, or 504, a request that got no response, and an attempt still unanswered after 30 seconds. AWS already retried through the AWS SDK and still leaves the retry mode and the attempt limit to it: the SDK reads `AWS_RETRY_MODE` and `AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS` first, then `retry_mode` and `max_attempts` in the selected profile, and otherwise uses standard mode with 3 attempts. That holds for every client the tools build, including the STS and SSO clients the credential providers create. Even when the settings allow a single attempt, a refused connection or a DNS failure is reported as unanswered, with a network next step, not as a permission refusal. When a read runs out of retries, Azure findings and the three access checks say the result is incomplete and recommend waiting for the service or restoring network access instead of a grant. The Azure and Google Cloud access checks still set their status from readable probes alone, so `healthy` can appear beside that note.
- **Which server errors are retried.** Box, CrowdStrike, Datadog, Google Workspace, LaunchDarkly, MuleSoft, PagerDuty, Qualys, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Snowflake, Splunk, Tenable, Veracode, and Zendesk retry every status of 500 and above. The other 17, including Azure, Google Cloud, AWS, Okta, Zscaler, and Ansible Automation Platform, retry 500, 502, 503, and 504 but no other server error, so an answer such as 501 or 505 is sent once and fails the read.
- **Waits follow the server, up to a cap.** Each wait follows the delay the server asks for, usually in a `Retry-After` header, or else backs off, and every wait is capped, at 15 to 60 seconds depending on the integration. When a server asks for longer than the cap, Ansible Automation Platform, Azure, Cloudflare, Duo, GitHub, Google Cloud, Google Workspace, LaunchDarkly, MuleSoft, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce, Slack, Splunk, Vanta, Webex, Zoom, and Zscaler fail the read at once, and the error names the wait the server asked for, since a retry before then is likely to be refused again. The others wait the capped time and retry, except AWS, whose waits are the AWS SDK's own backoff: the SDK honors a `Retry-After` or `x-amz-retry-after` header only up to 5 seconds past that delay. Before, Duo, GitHub, Palo Alto Networks, and Salesforce slept through whatever wait a server asked for. A requested wait too far off to represent as a date, which made GitHub, Slack, Zoom, and Webex fail with a bare `RangeError: Invalid time value`, now gets each client's own error, which says the wait ends past the latest representable date.
- **Requests that could hang now time out.** GitHub, Okta, Google Workspace, Vanta, Azure, Google Cloud, and AWS requests had no time limit of their own, so a stalled request waited until the tool call was stopped. Each attempt now gets 30 seconds, and an AWS attempt also gets 10 seconds to connect. In most of the 32 integrations, Azure and Google Cloud included, the timeout also covers reading the response body, so a body that stalls after the headers is retried like any other timeout. AWS's 30 seconds run until the service starts answering.
- **A read that still fails is reported as unread.** When the attempts run out, the error names the request, the last status or failure, and the attempt count, for example `Zoom request failed for GET /v2/users after 4 attempts: timed out after 30000 ms`. The data that request was reading is reported as unread, never as empty or complete, even when the failure lands on a later page, so no check passes on a partial inventory. A stopped tool call is not retried, and stopping during a retry wait ends it at once.
- **Public data feeds.** The KEV, EPSS, CMVP, SCF, and FedRAMP tools retry the public feeds they read, up to 4 attempts of 30 seconds each, and label what is missing when the retries run out. `kevs_get_epss` shows `Unavailable` instead of `Not scored` for CVE IDs whose EPSS batch failed and adds `(incomplete)` to its heading, and when every batch fails it returns an error instead of `No EPSS scores found`. `kevs_search` and `kevs_recent` show EPSS as `Unavailable` where the EPSS line used to be missing. `scf_get_control` names each evidence request that failed. FedRAMP results say when the GitHub metadata could not be read, and an empty `fedramp_search_frmr` result says when it came from a stale cache.
- **Checks that passed on partial data.** Splunk SPLUNK-AUD-17 now warns when a later page of `audit.conf` returns 404. Before, it read the file as absent and passed on the documented default. Okta OKTA-INTEG-004 is Partial beside a contextual policy rule, or Manual without one, when the network zone read fails, and Duo DUO-AUTH-010 stops at Partial when the WebAuthn credential inventory failed or stopped early and an enrolled user has a WebAuthn credential. Before, both could pass. Cloudflare CF-TRF-06 (Gateway rules) and CF-TRF-02 (page rules) no longer pass when the response says it holds only some of the rules or pages. Azure AZURE-MON-06 now stops at `warn` when the diagnostic settings list is truncated, as it already did for a truncated workspace list.
- **Incomplete Vanta exports say so.** When an evidence download or file listing fails, `vanta_export_audit` reports `as an incomplete package` with a reason. `_audit_info.json` carries `complete: false` and an `incomplete_evidence` list, and each item in `metadata.json` and `_index.csv` carries an `export_status` of `complete`, `files_missing`, or `urls_unknown`. A download that sends nothing for 30 seconds or breaks off partway is recorded, and its partial file is removed. Before, such an export read as a normal export with a warning count.
- **Tenable exports.** Status polls and chunk downloads are retried, and a chunk's timeout restarts as each piece of the body arrives, so a large chunk that keeps arriving is not cut off. Each attempt may run 20 times `TENABLE_TIMEOUT`, 10 minutes at the default. The request that starts an export is not resent after a timeout or network failure, because Tenable may already have started that export. That export is then unreadable and its controls are `manual`. A chunk that fails on every attempt marks the export truncated, so no control passes on the chunks that did arrive.
- **Token requests and sessions.** Token requests are retried too. Box and Okta sign a fresh client assertion for each token attempt, since both refuse a reused one, and Duo signs each attempt again with a new `Date`. A prebuilt Okta assertion, passed as `client_assertion` or `OKTA_CLIENT_CLIENTASSERTION`, can be used only once, so it is sent once. If that attempt fails in a way that would otherwise be retried, the error says it was not retried and to rerun with a fresh assertion or with a private key in its place. After its one token refresh on a 401, GitHub reuses the refreshed installation token instead of minting another on every retry. A Zoom token exchange or Webex refresh grant that fails is not sent again in the same tool call, so a token endpoint that stays down costs one round of retries instead of one per surface, and concurrent Webex reads share one grant. Azure reads that start together share one token request per resource, and Google Cloud access probes share one token exchange, retries included. Ansible Automation Platform never resends its session login after a timeout, since that could expire the user's oldest session. Snowflake resends a statement only with its original `requestId` and `retry=true`, so the SQL API runs it once.
- **GitHub and Google Workspace rate limits.** When a GitHub rate limit names no wait, the GitHub tools now wait the one minute GitHub asks for, where they waited 250 ms, and a repeat on the same request fails, since GitHub then asks for longer than the 60-second cap. Google Workspace retries a 403 whose reason is `userRateLimitExceeded`, `rateLimitExceeded`, or `quotaExceeded`, and one that outlasts the retries is reported as a request error, never as a missing scope or admin role. A direct access token's 401 is final instead of being resent four times.
- **Palo Alto Networks devices that stop answering.** Once a PAN-OS device gives no answer after its retries, its remaining reads in that tool call fail at once without being sent, with `was not attempted because <device> did not answer an earlier request`. An offline device costs about 2 minutes per collection, and other devices are unaffected.

## Access checks name rejected credentials

- **`failed`, not `limited`.** When a vendor refuses the credentials themselves, 29 access checks now report `failed` and name the settings to fix. Before, they reported `limited` and asked for permissions, scopes, or roles that would not have helped. The 29 are Azure, Box, Cloudflare, CrowdStrike, Duo, Elastic, GitHub, Google Cloud, Google Workspace, KnowBe4, LaunchDarkly, MuleSoft, New Relic, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Okta, PagerDuty, Palo Alto Networks, Qualys, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Snowflake, Splunk, Sumo Logic, Tenable, Veracode, Webex, Zendesk, Zoom, and Zscaler. Palo Alto Networks reported `degraded` before.
- **The next step names the variable.** For example, `GitHub rejected the token (every probe returned 401). Set GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN or pass api_token with a valid token, then rerun github_check_access.` Each step follows the auth mode in use, names the aliases the resolver also reads, and names the region, cloud, or platform setting wherever a credential sent to the wrong host draws the same refusal. A `failed` result lists no missing permissions, and its notes say permissions were not checked.
- **Permission gaps are unchanged.** A 403, one readable probe, or a failure that is not a credential refusal, such as a 429 or a 5xx, keeps the `healthy`, `limited`, or `degraded` result from `v0.1.3`. The new messages hold only fixed text, setting names, and status or vendor error codes, never response text.
- **Slack, Datadog, AWS, and GitHub App.** A rejected Slack token names `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` and its alias `SLACK_TOKEN`, or `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` when only a bot token is set. Datadog no longer lists all 17 permissions as missing when it rejects the API or application key. When AWS finds no credentials, the error says to set `AWS_PROFILE` or run `aws sso login`. A GitHub App installation token request that returns 404 reports `failed` and says the installation ID is wrong or the App is not installed.

## First run

- **`grclanker --version`** prints the version, as do `-v` and `grclanker version`. `grclanker help` works like `--help`.
- **Session resume.** `grclanker --session <id>`, the command grclanker prints when you leave a session, reopens that session. `v0.1.3` rejected it as an unknown option. `/resume` inside a session works as before.
- **No terminal, no silent exit.** Started from a script or CI job before setup has run, `grclanker` exits `1` with `grclanker is not configured yet, and first-run setup needs an interactive terminal.`, and `grclanker setup` exits `1` and says no model was configured. Both point to the settings file and the [Configuration](https://grclanker.com/docs/getting-started/configuration/) guide. Before, the first launch printed a stack trace, and setup exited `0` without saving anything.
- **Setup hints.** Local-first setup says to start Ollama with `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=128000`, since grclanker sends about 100k tokens of tool definitions with each request and Ollama's default context window is too small to hold them. Hosted setup names the API key variable grclanker reads: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or `GEMINI_API_KEY`.
- **Flue.** When `grclanker flue run` stops at `Provider is not configured: <provider>`, it now names the API key variable to set, or says to point `GRCLANKER_FLUE_MODEL` at a provider you have a key for.

## KEV

- **Exact CVE first.** `kevs_search` puts the entry whose CVE ID equals the query first. Before, catalog order could put another entry ahead of it: asking for `CVE-2021-44228` with `limit: 1` returned `CVE-2021-45046`, whose description cites it, and `CVE-2022-2294` returned `CVE-2022-22948`.
- **Full counts.** When `limit` leaves entries out, `kevs_search` and `kevs_recent` replies start with `Showing N of M`, and `details.total_matches` carries the full count. Before, the heading counted only the rows shown. Replies that show every match are unchanged.

## Tools match their docs

- **Zendesk ZD-05** fails when mobile app access is on and the mobile app session timeout is 0 (never expires) or more than three times the threshold, as the docs say. Before, only the agent timeout could fail the check, and a mobile timeout like that only warned. Exactly three times the threshold still warns.
- **LaunchDarkly** caveats for a truncated listing name only arguments that raise that listing's cap. Team roles, members in access control, custom roles in environment governance, and environments in flag hygiene and monitoring are read at a fixed cap, so those caveats now say to review the uncollected items manually. Before, they advised `role_limit`, `member_limit`, or `environment_limit`, and a rerun with a higher value returned the same truncated result.
- **AWS** names the IAM actions S3 needs: `s3:ListAllMyBuckets`, `s3:GetBucketPublicAccessBlock`, and `s3:GetEncryptionConfiguration`. Before, its permission list held the API operation names `s3:ListBuckets`, `s3:GetPublicAccessBlock`, and `s3:GetBucketEncryption`, so a policy built from that list did not allow those calls. `aws_check_access` records `s3:ListAllMyBuckets` for its S3 probe, and error lines still name the API call that failed.
- **SCF.** `scf_get_crosswalk` advertises its real default of 10 rows in each direction, and a call that skips argument preparation now uses 10 instead of 8.
- **Okta OSCAL.** CI checks the FedRAMP assessment results in `okta_export_audit_bundle` against the NIST OSCAL 1.1.2 assessment-results schema, using bundles from six fixture orgs. The builder now leaves out empty `observations` and `findings` lists, which the schema rejects. No bundle produced them, so bundle output is unchanged.

## Durable mode and stopped exports

- **Sessions from a newer grclanker are refused with a message.** `grclanker durable` reads a session's schema version over a read-only connection before Pi Durable opens it. A session at a newer schema version exits `1` with `Session "<id>" was written by a newer grclanker`, both schema versions, and `The session was not changed.` instead of a stack trace. A `session.sqlite` that is not a SQLite database gets its own message. Neither file is opened for writing.
- **Vanta.** A stop that lands while `vanta_export_audit` is downloading an evidence file now settles only after that file is closed, so the export's staging directory is removed cleanly.

## Installers and bundles

- **A failed upgrade keeps the old install.** Both installers move the previous install aside, extract into a fresh directory, and put the previous install back if extraction fails, then exit non-zero with `Could not extract <bundle>, so the previous install was restored` (shell) or `Extraction failed, so the previous install was restored.` (PowerShell). Before, a corrupt archive, a full disk, or an interrupted extraction could leave no working `grclanker`.
- **Unreadable archives stop first.** The shell installer stops with `Could not list the entries in <bundle>, so nothing was installed` when `tar` cannot list a bundle, before it moves anything. Before, a truncated bundle passed the entry check on a partial listing.
- **A failed skills install keeps the installed skill.** `install-skills` and `install-skills.ps1` download `SKILL.md` beside the installed copy, check that it is the grclanker skill, and only then replace the installed one. A cut-off download, a sign-in page, or a missing version exits non-zero with `Could not download <url>, so nothing was changed` or `<url> did not return a grclanker SKILL.md, so nothing was changed`, and a failed first install leaves no empty skill directory. Before, a cut-off download left part of the file, a sign-in page replaced the skill with HTML, and the installers could still exit `0`.
- **Faster Windows installs.** `install.ps1` extracts the bundle's 39,020 files with one .NET `ZipFile` call instead of `Expand-Archive`. The Windows PowerShell 5.1 install job in CI went from 3m30s to 1m26s.
- **License files.** Every bundle carries the Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` and `NOTICE` under `app/`. The `v0.1.3` bundles did not.
- The site serves the installers from `main`, so these changes are already live: the three CLI installer changes since October 22 and the skills installer change since October 23. The license files arrive with the `v0.1.4` bundles.

## Release pipeline

- **Every bundle runs on its own platform before it is published.** Bundles are cross-built on Linux. The release workflow now installs each of the six with the real installer on a native runner: macOS on Apple silicon and Intel, Linux on arm64 and x64, and Windows on arm64 and x64 under both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7. Each install has to verify its checksum, run a Node.js built for its platform, and print the same tool count as the Linux build. A release gate refuses to publish unless every check passes, and `v0.1.4` is the first release published through it.
- Pull requests and pushes to `main` that touch the bundle builder, the installers, or the CLI entry run the same checks and publish nothing.
- **Weekly checks.** The same checks run on `main` every Monday, so a retired or broken runner image fails a run nobody is waiting on instead of the next release. Scheduled runs publish nothing.
- **Live smoke tests stop on rejected credentials.** The MuleSoft, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Palo Alto Networks, Qualys, Snowflake, Sumo Logic, Tenable, Veracode, Webex, and Zscaler live smoke scripts exit `1` with the access check's next step when it reports `failed`, instead of running assessments against a tenant they cannot read and reporting a pass.
- **Live smoke tests run with every credential the tools accept.** The Box, Google Cloud, ServiceNow, and Slack live smoke scripts skipped when set up with a credential their tool accepts, such as `BOX_TOKEN`, `GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN` with `GCLOUD_PROJECT`, `SERVICENOW_INSTANCE_URL`, `SLACK_TOKEN`, or Slack's default config file. They now run, and their skip messages list every credential that counts.
- CI splits the CLI tests into three shards balanced by measured run time, and stops with an error when PowerShell is missing instead of skipping the 16 PowerShell installer tests. The checks are unchanged.

## Docs and site

- **Lighter pages on phones.** Phones get right-sized images, and the homepage drops from 714 KB to 424 KB. Hashed scripts are cached for a year, fonts for 30 days, and images for a day, and fonts start loading with the page. Homepage card titles now keep at least 4.6:1 contrast over every brand picture, and the hero's links are underlined instead of told apart by color alone.
- **First-run docs.** The README and Quick Start run `grclanker tools` before the first session and explain how to leave and resume one. Installation and Setup document Ollama's context length and the first session's download of `fd` and `rg`, with `PI_OFFLINE=1` for machines without internet access.
- **Integration docs match the CLI.** The pages for 21 integrations and Compute Backends now describe what the shipped tools do, including Salesforce's `private_key` argument, Snowflake's polling and retry settings, Azure's `healthy` threshold of six of eight readable probes, 13 rows of the Qualys verdict table, LaunchDarkly's fixed caps, the status codes Zscaler retries, and each live smoke script's skip and exit rules. The Palo Alto Networks spec names `~/.grclanker/paloalto.json`, the file the tools read, as the default config file.
- **Docs checked against the CLI.** The site build fails when a docs page or the README names a tool the CLI does not define, or sets or lists an environment variable the code never mentions.
- **Four runtime paths.** The homepage counts the experimental durable runtime as a fourth runtime path.
- Integration pages describe the `failed` access status and the next step each check prints.
- **Retry docs.** The pages for the 32 integrations that retry, the KEV / EPSS page, and the SCF and FedRAMP guides describe the retry limits, the error text, and what a read that runs out of retries does to a verdict.

## Security

- **`hono` 4.13.13**, up from 4.13.8, fixes GHSA-5r4p-p66f-jhc7 (medium). The bundle carries `hono` through the Flue runtime.
- **`ip-address` 10.7.4**, up from 10.7.2, fixes GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5 (medium), published October 22. The bundle carries `ip-address` through `@earendil-works/pi-ai`.
- Source checkouts pin `@modelcontextprotocol/server` to 2.3.1, which fixes GHSA-jm63-cq47-j5jp, GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453, and GHSA-rvq5-wwqv-78pq. It is a development dependency and is not in the bundle.
- `npm audit` for the CLI still reports the 2 high advisories from `v0.1.3`, both GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv in `node-forge`, counted once directly and once through `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime`. No patched `node-forge` exists yet. The site has none.

## Upgrade notes

- Rerun the installer to upgrade. Settings and runtime state under `~/.grclanker/agent` are kept.
- Source checkouts should rerun `npm --prefix cli ci`, since the CLI lockfile changed.
- **Slower failures from hosts that never answer.** Timeouts are now retried, so a host that accepts connections but never answers costs up to five timeouts by default, plus the waits between them, before a read is reported as failed: up to about three minutes at a 30-second timeout. Most integrations take a timeout setting, and Box, Datadog, Qualys, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Snowflake, and Zscaler also take a retry count. AWS takes its attempt limit from `AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS` or the profile's `max_attempts`. Each integration page lists them.
- **Error text.** An error for a request that ran out of retries now names the attempt count, such as `after 4 attempts`, and Box and Zendesk errors no longer include the query string. Anything that matches the old error text needs the new wording.
- **Results that change.** Expect `warn` for Splunk SPLUNK-AUD-17 and Azure AZURE-MON-06, Partial or Manual for Okta OKTA-INTEG-004, Partial for Duo DUO-AUTH-010, and no pass for Cloudflare CF-TRF-06 and CF-TRF-02 where `v0.1.3` passed on data it could not fully read. `kevs_get_epss` shows `Unavailable` instead of `Not scored` for a CVE ID whose EPSS batch failed. In a Vanta export package, an item whose file list could not be read has `files: null` instead of `[]`, and new `complete`, `incomplete_evidence`, and `export_status` fields say what is missing.
- **Tenable.** An attempt still receiving its response after 20 times `TENABLE_TIMEOUT` now fails and marks the export truncated, where `v0.1.3` kept reading. For a slow link, raise `TENABLE_TIMEOUT`, up to 600 seconds, which raises the cap with it.
- **AWS profiles.** A profile chosen with the `profile` argument now applies all of its client settings, the same way `AWS_PROFILE` does: its `retry_mode` and `max_attempts`, and settings such as `use_fips_endpoint`, `use_dualstack_endpoint`, and the S3 checksum settings. Before, those settings came from `AWS_PROFILE` or the default profile. `endpoint_url` still comes from `AWS_PROFILE` or the default profile.
- Expect `failed` where `v0.1.3` reported `limited`, or `degraded` for Palo Alto Networks, when a vendor rejects the credentials. Scripts and reports that read the access status should treat `failed` as a credential problem. Accepted credentials report as before.
- Expect `fail` where `v0.1.3` reported `warn` for Zendesk ZD-05 when mobile app access is on and the mobile app session timeout is 0 or more than three times the threshold.
- If you built an IAM policy from the S3 actions the AWS tools listed in `v0.1.3`, replace `s3:ListBuckets`, `s3:GetPublicAccessBlock`, and `s3:GetBucketEncryption` with `s3:ListAllMyBuckets`, `s3:GetBucketPublicAccessBlock`, and `s3:GetEncryptionConfiguration`.
- `kevs_search` and `kevs_recent` replies cut by `limit` start with `Showing N of M` instead of `Found N` or `N KEV entries added`. Anything that parses those headings should read `details.total_matches` instead.
- **Durable sessions.** This release still pins pi-durable 1.3.0, so the `v0.1.3` note about the next pi-durable still applies: once a later release migrates a session, neither `v0.1.3` nor `v0.1.4` can open it. `v0.1.4` refuses it with a message and leaves the file unchanged. If you might go back, copy `~/.grclanker/durable/sessions/` before opening your sessions with a newer release.

Full changelog: [What's New](https://grclanker.com/docs/changelog/) and [v0.1.3...v0.1.4](https://github.com/ethanolivertroy/grclanker/compare/v0.1.3...v0.1.4).
